title: Pathology: nuclei annotation to 2D U-Net learning

steps.prompt: Create a project called "Pathology golden story"
steps.action: Create a fresh project for nuclei segmentation; cell-type classification is a separate task.

steps.prompt: Open the dataset import form
steps.action: Import bounded RGB fields from at least two independent source slides. Assign entire slides/patients to training or validation; crops from one slide never cross splits.

steps.prompt: Open the API credential form
steps.action: Configure a server environment reference or encrypted credential for the hosted annotation model.

steps.prompt: Show the annotation model connection form
steps.action: Configure Sol or a nuclei segmentation endpoint. Sol is the default hosted choice; Astra requires explicit selection.

steps.prompt: View this sample in QuPath
steps.action: Select a training image in Datasets first. QuPath opens with the MONAI Label tab.

steps.prompt: Use Sol for annotation from now on
steps.action: In the open QuPath MONAI Label tab, select Sol for future annotation requests. The coordinator remains independent from the annotation model.

steps.prompt: Run nuclei segmentation on the selected region using Sol
steps.action: Draw one area in QuPath. It is sent as one crop without tiling; outside objects are preserved.

steps.prompt: Run nuclei segmentation on the whole image using Sol with tile size 512
steps.action: Optional whole-image route. It overrides an active selection and processes bounded imported images in tiles; streaming gigapixel slides is not implemented.

steps.prompt: Classify the annotated nuclei into tumor, immune and stromal
steps.action: Optional: confirm categories and inspect candidate cell types. Classification drafts are local; this story trains nuclei masks, not a cell-type classifier.

steps.prompt: Submit this annotation for review
steps.action: Check the complete imported field before submitting. A small selected region alone is not a complete training label.

steps.prompt: Show the pending review queue
steps.action: Open a submitted sample in QuPath as reviewer. Pending is the default queue filter.

steps.prompt: Accept my corrected segmentation
steps.action: Review/edit in QuPath, then accept the corrected mask. Repeat for training fields and independently reviewed held-out slides.

steps.prompt: Create a snapshot of the reviewed dataset
steps.action: Freeze full accepted masks and disjoint source groups.

steps.prompt: Create a U-Net segmentation model named Nuclei U-Net for nuclei from scratch; do not start training yet
steps.action: The same recipe infers 2D RGB input from the imported pathology images. VISTA3D is a CT model and is not used for pathology.

steps.prompt: Train the selected project learner
steps.action: Train version 1; keep its checkpoint for the later comparison. Small quick-start runs verify software, not clinical quality.

steps.prompt: Annotate nuclei on the full image using the selected model
steps.action: Refresh and select the trained U-Net in QuPath. Annotate a new training field, correct it, submit and accept it; do not use validation slides for learning.

steps.prompt: Continue training the selected model on the reviewed dataset
steps.action: Select version 1 and its learner. Continue on a new snapshot of the expanded reviewed dataset; version 2 preserves parent/optimizer lineage.

steps.prompt: Compare the selected new model against the selected previous version on the current held-out snapshot
steps.action: Set version 2 as candidate and version 1 as baseline. Run both on the same held-out slide groups.

steps.prompt: Show the held-out evaluation results
steps.action: Inspect nuclei Dice for both versions and their difference. Do not assume the new model is better.

steps.prompt: Annotate nuclei in the selected region using the selected model
steps.action: Refresh and select version 2 explicitly only after reviewing the comparison. Project-wide promotion remains a separate guarded action.
